record.paper_title: 二分決定グラフに基づく計算複雑さに関する未解決問題について
record.original_question: Let LogCut be the class of Boolean functions computable by polynomial-size circuit families whose underlying directed acyclic circuit graphs have cutwidth O(log n), and let NL be nondeterministic logarithmic-space computation. Is LogCut a proper subclass of NL, or does LogCut equal NL?

evidence.quote: カット幅が入力のサイズ n に対し O(log n) である多項式サイズ回路族で計算できる関数のクラスを LogCut と書く。
LogCut は、L を真に含み NL に含まれるが、NL に真に含まれるかどうかはわかっていない。

artifact.self_contained_problem: Define LogCut to be the class of Boolean functions f : {0,1}* → {0,1} such that there exists a polynomial-size family {C_n} of Boolean circuits computing f, with the additional property that the underlying directed acyclic graph of C_n has cutwidth O(log n). (The cutwidth of a DAG is the minimum, over all linear orderings of its vertices, of the maximum number of edges crossing any "cut" between consecutive positions in the ordering.) Let L denote deterministic logarithmic-space and NL denote nondeterministic logarithmic-space computation. It is known that L ⊊ LogCut ⊆ NL. Determine whether LogCut = NL or LogCut ⊊ NL.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of the LogCut vs. NL question was found. Searches for the class LogCut and its relation to nondeterministic logspace return only general background on NL and space-bounded complexity, with no indication that the strict-inclusion question has been settled. Given that even L vs. NL remains open, this finer question is also believed to remain open.

status_evidence.title: NL (complexity) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of NL and its standard relationships to L and other classes; no mention of a resolution comparing cutwidth-bounded circuit classes to NL.
status_evidence.claim: Standard relations among L, NL and circuit classes are surveyed but the LogCut vs. NL question is not reported as resolved.
